question: What starting values and month-to-month persistence should the game's simulated national economy use (unemployment, inflation, growth, the policy rate, and the probability of a normal year versus a downturn or a shock), and on what real calendar are unemployment, CPI and GDP figures released?

sourcesChecked.whatItDidNotSettle: Values are labelled provisional; release day is unmarked.
Covers real published county and state figures, not the simulated national series.

title: The simulated economy's starting values, its month-to-month rules, and when its figures are published
usableAnswer: Long-run ranges for the anchors and persistence from published series (FRED is fine), the historical frequency of recessions as a basis for regime weights, and the standard release schedule for the three figures.
whyItMatters: The macro-conditions panel and the budget workspace show a simulated economy built from invented anchors. At main 9f42ba19: src/simulation/macro-economy/policy.ts:12-63 holds regime weights 0.7/0.25/0.05, a 2% growth anchor, persistence 0.85 and 0.95, and shock sizes labelled 'director-authored-provisional' and 'CHANGE-authored placeholders' with no question id. src/simulation/macro-economy/producer.ts:66 publishes all three headline figures on the first of the following month, when BLS and BEA each release on their own lag (jobs report first Friday; CPI mid-month; GDP advance estimate about a month after quarter end). The policy-effect answer (policy-effect-model-state-and-local) confirmed these 'placeholders are not confirmed' but supplied no values.
